chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Humran ibn A'yan from one of the Imams (peace be upon them) said:
My father, when he prayed sitting, would sit in the tarrabba' position; and when he bowed (ruku'), he would bend his legs.

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And it is sufficient for the sick person and the hurried one to pray in the first two rak'at of their obligatory prayers with Surah al-Hamd alone. Until his saying: 'And whoever forgets an obligatory prayer.' All of that has already been explained, so there is no need to repeat it. Then he said (may Allah have mercy on him): And whoever forgets an obligatory prayer, let him make it up at any time he remembers it, as long as it is not the end time of the second prayer, such that the second prayer is missed by the making up.

key_terms.تَرَبَّعَ: To sit in a specific posture with legs bent or spread

ai.seo_question: What is the correct posture for sitting prayer and how to make up missed prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific *tarrabba'* posture for sitting prayer, where the legs are folded during bowing, reflecting the practical adaptations of the Imams. Shaykh al-Tusi supplements this with a juristic ruling that the sick and hurried may suffice with Surah al-Hamd alone in the first two rak'ahs, and clarifies that missed obligatory prayers (*fara'id*) must be made up at any time, provided they do not overlap with the time of the next prayer. This highlights the Shia emphasis on ease (*taysir*) in worship while maintaining strict adherence to the sequence of obligations.
